analysis: This PR is documentation-only: hardware-support.md (the supplied head text is the unchanged tail; the diff adds a selected-model recovery section near head lines 371-408, and I saw only a truncated patch excerpt of it) and model-autopilot.md (diff plus base text). No executable code, wire protocol, key custody, attestation, or encryption path changes in the supplied evidence. The prose describes provider-local selected-model recovery behavior: a retry loop with allowEviction:false, eviction of only idle, unheld, unpinned adopted models that meet the operation victim rules, and release of an adoption ten minutes after a hold or wait. It also adds invariant 10, a restart-needed note for enabled_models, and an add-on hold pause that cancels a recovery attempt. Relevant threats: T-059 and T-060 (add-on hold DoS), A-018 (serving availability), and the Autopilot consent and lease controls in TB-011/T-052. From the documentation, recovery gates on existing controls: consent, Autopilot pins, holds, leases, min_dwell, evictionExclusions and the add-on hold. It does not appear to widen coordinator control or bypass Autopilot consent. The documented adoption release does let the provider unilaterally withdraw a coordinator-placed adoption, which is an availability-policy change rather than a confidentiality or integrity regression. The implementation (ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift, ProviderLoop+SelectedModelPlacementPolicy.swift) is not supplied and is labelled 'policy pending owner review', so I cannot verify that the doc's invariants hold in code, for example that recovery respects the add-on hold, never evicts models with in-flight requests, and handles the stale-selection restart note. The hardware-support.md patch excerpt is truncated, so the rest of that section was not seen. No concrete regression is supported by the evidence. A follow-up pass over the code diff, if one exists, should check recovery eviction against T-059/T-060 and the unload, retirement and wipe lifecycle.
